key_insight: Glioblastoma necrosis may be an active, mutation-driven process in which tumor-recruited neutrophils form extracellular traps and amplify HMGB2-linked tumor necroptosis.
clinical_relevance: MRI-measured necrosis and high HMGB2 expression may help identify high-risk glioblastoma, while the inflammatory cascade offers investigational therapeutic targets.
method: Integrated clinical MRI radiomics with public genomic datasets.
Mapped tumor niches using single-cell spatial transcriptomics.
Examined mechanisms using protein immunofluorescence in a TP53/PTEN/NF1 co-mutant mouse model.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports public genomic datasets totaling n=3,639, associations between MRI necrotic volume and poorer survival, and multi-cohort clinical validation of an HMGB2-high risk signature.
watch_item: Mechanistic and treatment findings are preclinical; prospective validation is needed before using these biomarkers or targets in patient care.
paper_title: Tumor Associated Neutrophils Extend NETs To Spatially Drive Necroptosis In Glioblastoma
